=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves are attached singly at different nodes along the stem, alternating sides as seen in images 1 and 4)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves appear to be grouped closely together at the shoot tips)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade without leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (leaf margins appear smooth without teeth or serrations)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (leaves are widest in the middle and taper gradually toward both ends)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (leaf tips taper to a distinct, elongated point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (leaf bases taper to a wedge-shaped point)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a central midrib is visible with secondary veins branching off)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): prominent and clearly visible (secondary veins are distinct and curve toward the leaf margin)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (leaf surfaces reflect light, indicating a smooth, glossy texture)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on the leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are visible but relatively short compared to the leaf blade)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles appear cylindrical and smooth without wings or grooves)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (the stems appear green and slender, typical of a young seedling)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on the stems)
    19. Stem color: green (stems are a consistent green color)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (stems appear smooth without obvious ridges or lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are visible at the leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex is visible)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no pulvinus is visible at the leaf bases)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils are visible)
F. Notes: The seedling has a pink tag attached to one of the leaves. Some leaves show minor damage, such as small holes or missing pieces of the margin.
